name: security-settings
title: Security settings
description: A security page: a checkup with Done, Recommended and At risk badges, password, two-factor with QR setup, passkeys, sessions and alerts.

useCases: Account security pages for SaaS and fintech apps
Two-factor setup with an authenticator app or text
Reviewing and signing out sessions and devices
Security checkups that nudge people to finish setup

a11y.reducedMotion: Nothing slides, grows or shakes: the checkup ring jumps to its value, rows and the password form appear without folding, dialogs only fade, the code boxes don't shake on a wrong code, and the checkup scrolls without smooth scrolling.

keyboard.action: Moves through the settings nav, the checkup fixes, every row's button, the password fields and the alert switches
Runs a fix from the checkup, opens the password form or a two-factor setup, signs a session out, or flips an alert
Types the 6-digit code; pasting a code or the browser's one-time-code autofill fills all six boxes
Closes a setup or confirm dialog without changing anything

notes: Status badges say Done, Recommended or At risk in words as well as colour, and the checkup summary (“2 at risk, 1 recommended”) is a polite live region.
A checkup fix moves focus to the section it scrolls to; after a two-factor setup started from the checkup, focus returns to the sign-in card because the button that opened it is gone.

Each password field has a visible label and a show/hide button named for it; the requirements are a list linked to the new password with `aria-describedby`, and each says done or not yet to screen readers.
Turning off two-factor, making new recovery codes and signing out every other session ask first, in a dialog that names the action and the count.
The 6-digit code is one real input (`autocomplete="one-time-code"`) behind the boxes, so screen readers and autofill see a single field.
gaps: The QR code has a text alternative (the setup key, shown and copyable), but the image itself can't be read by screen readers. (WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content)
Flags in the country list are emoji; on systems without flag emoji they show as two-letter codes. (WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content)
